la:verb:dinumero.html:
dī-nŭmĕro, āvi, ātum, 1,
v. a., to count over, reckon up, enumerate.
In gen. (class.): stellas,: annos,; cf. horas,: tempora, * : noctes,: syllabas (c. c. dimetiri),: spoliata templa,: exercitum,: generis gradus,.—Absol.: centuriat Capuae, dinumerat,—
In Plaut. and Ter. in partic., mercantile t. t., to count out, pay out money: argentum,; ; : hibus stipendium,; cf.: viginti minas illi,.

la:noun:dine.html:
dīnē, es, f., = δίνη,
a whirlwind: vertex ille est, vel uti dicitur dine, etc., Ap. de Mundo, 12, p. 62, 32 (dub. Hild. Helicias).

la:noun:dinumeratio.html:
dīnŭmĕrātĭo, ōnis, f.
id.
,
a counting over, reckoning up, enumeration.
In gen. (very rare): noctium ac dierum,; cf. (dierum),: (personarum),; .—
Esp., as a figure of speech, i. q. Gr. ἀπαρίθμησις, ; quoted ap. (who, however, does not regard it as a figure); 9, 3, 91 Spald.

la:verb:dinosco.html:
dī-nosco (old form, dīgnosco—no
perf. nor sup.), ĕre, 3, v. a.
dis, 2.; nosco
, to know apart, to distinguish, discern one thing from another (perh. not ante-Aug.).
With ab: vix ut dinosci possit a mastiche verā,. —
With abl.: civem dinoscere hoste,: ut possem curvo dinoscere rectum,: aera tinnitu,: vocem auribus, speciem oculis,: aliquid sapore,.—
With accus.: suos et alienos,: vera bona,: veri speciem,.—
With rel. clause: dinoscere Quid solidum crepet, etc.,.—(ε) Absol.: inter se similes, vix ut dinoscere possis,; .
